name: Route selection
legal_basis: No statutory basis. The 2021 baseline fieldwork was itself screened by the Review Board and followed a speculative corridor from the draft land use plan.
takes_in: Engineering and cost constraints; traditional land use and Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit studies; whatever input the proponent chooses to seek.
can_produce: A preferred corridor and a short list of alternatives.
assessment_method_label: Weighted scoring — numbers assigned and combined
assessment_method_note: Assumed to use weighted multi-criteria siting of the kind standard in transmission routing. Not confirmed for this project — and if confirmed, it is the only place on the map where incommensurable things are given numbers and added.
kind_label: Framing — fixes what later steps can argue about
note: The only step with no public record, and everything downstream traces back to it.

name: Transmission service request
legal_basis: Manitoba Hydro's open access transmission tariff. The governing provision has not been read.
takes_in: A request for up to 150 MW and a point of interconnection.
can_produce: Feasibility; required system upgrades.
assessment_method_note: Power-system modelling. A genuinely technical question with a determinate answer.
note: Filed 4 November 2025. The filing is confirmed; the tariff basis is not.

name: Federal funding channels
legal_basis: Programme terms rather than statute.
takes_in: Project economics, strategic rationale, Indigenous participation.
can_produce: Contributions with conditions; prioritisation.
assessment_method_note: No published appraisal method. Decisions appear as announcements rather than as assessments.
note: Wide intake, no assessment, almost nothing published. Runs throughout rather than stopping here.

name: Cabinet designation
legal_basis: Canadian Energy Regulator Act s.261. Federal law treats Nunavut as a province, so the line very likely is an interprovincial power line.
takes_in: Cabinet consideration.
can_produce: Designate, or do not designate.
assessment_method_note: No criteria are published and no timeline applies. The decision is not an assessment of anything.
note: The entire federal lane hangs on this one order. None has been made, and nothing has to happen before one could be.

name: Environment Act Proposal
legal_basis: The Environment Act ss.11–12; Classes of Development Regulation 164/88; Licensing Procedures Regulation 163/88.
takes_in: Project description, environmental assessment, alternatives considered.
can_produce: Filed as complete, or further information required.
decider: Director or Minister, depending on class
assessment_method_label: Completeness or conformity check against written criteria
assessment_method_note: Completeness against the regulation's content requirements, including mapping at 1:50,000 or better.
note: Above 230 kV is Class 3 and the Minister decides; 115 to 230 kV is Class 2 and the Director does. The voltage has not been published, so the whole Manitoba lane's shape is undetermined.

name: Planning conformity
legal_basis: NuPPAA ss.76–85, with s.156 applying the planning provisions to the entire project.
takes_in: Project description and location.
can_produce: Conforms; does not conform; variance; or exemption.
assessment_method_label: Completeness or conformity check against written criteria
assessment_method_note: Conformity against the text of the applicable land use plan. A yes or no question about a document.
note: Tested against the regional plan, since the 2023 territory-wide plan was jointly rejected in July 2026.

name: Energy Regulator review
legal_basis: Canadian Energy Regulator Act ss.2, 261 and 262, with reasons under s.63. Removed from the Impact Assessment Act's list by SOR/2026-185 on 3 September 2026.
takes_in: Engineering, routing, environmental and socio-economic effects, Indigenous consultation.
can_produce: Certificate or permit with conditions, or refusal.
decider: The Commission and Governor in Council
assessment_method_note: A public interest determination on a hearing record. Inactive here.
note: Would be the widest single federal forum available. Inactive because nobody has made the designation order.

name: Public registry and comment
legal_basis: The Environment Act s.17, with ss.11(8)(a) and 12(4)(a).
takes_in: Written submissions from anyone. No content filter appears in the Act.
can_produce: Comments on the record; objections that may prompt a hearing.
written_reasons: Owed to objectors where no hearing is held (s.12(6))
assessment_method_note: None. Submissions are collected, not assessed. Nothing filters what may be said and nothing determines what follows.
note: Everything can come in and nothing goes out — but s.12(6) compels reasons for the decision NOT to hold a hearing.

name: Technical Advisory Committee
legal_basis: Administrative practice. Only a general advisory committee power at s.5.
takes_in: The proposal, reviewed by each department within its own mandate.
can_produce: Departmental comments and recommended licence conditions.
assessment_method_label: Expert judgment within a single mandate
assessment_method_note: Each department applies its own expertise to its own mandate. There is no step at which the departmental views are weighed against one another.
note: Each department answers within its mandate. Nothing holds several mandates together.

name: Crown–Indigenous consultation
legal_basis: Section 35 of the Constitution Act 1982 and provincial policy, which has not been retrieved.
takes_in: Potential adverse impacts on asserted or established rights.
can_produce: A consultation record and accommodation.
assessment_method_note: A legal test turning on the strength of the claim and the seriousness of the impact. Concerns not attaching to a right fall outside it however strongly held.
note: A rights channel, not a values channel.

name: Screening
legal_basis: NuPPAA ss.86–92 and 157. Section 90(i) makes cumulative impacts mandatory. Section 75(1) bars any regulatory authority from issuing a permit until assessment is complete, and s.75(2) makes any such permit of no force or effect.
takes_in: The proposal plus public and agency comments.
can_produce: Review not required; review required; or the project must be modified or abandoned.
assessment_method_note: A threshold judgment: may the project have significant ecosystemic or socio-economic impacts. Socio-economic sits in the test itself, which is the sharpest contrast with Manitoba.
note: The only confirmed hard gate on the map, and wider than first recorded: a permit issued in breach is void, not merely irregular.

name: Minister's screening decision
legal_basis: NuPPAA ss.93 and 94. Section 94(1)(a)(ii) makes a federal panel the default where the project is partly outside Nunavut.
takes_in: The Board's screening report.
can_produce: Proceed; review by the Board, a federal panel or a joint panel; or not proceed.
assessment_method_note: No published method. The Minister may send a project to review even where the Board found none necessary, and chooses the review body.
note: Who reviews the project is a discretionary choice made before the review begins.

name: Clean Environment Commission hearing
legal_basis: The Environment Act ss.6(5)(b), 12(6) and 7(3). Referral is discretionary; the report is due within 90 days.
takes_in: Evidence, public presentations, Information Requests, cross-examination.
can_produce: A public report with recommendations.
public_record: Yes — reports public, transcripts by practice
written_reasons: Yes, where recommendations are not incorporated
assessment_method_note: Adversarial hearing with Information Requests and cross-examination. Among the few methods able to hold several considerations in view at once — and it produces advice, not a decision.
note: Broad admissibility and compelled reasons on departure — and entirely optional.

name: Scoping and guidelines
legal_basis: NuPPAA ss.99 and 101. Draft guidelines must be in both official languages and in Inuktitut, which includes Inuinnaqtun.
takes_in: Public and agency input on what the assessment should cover.
can_produce: Guidelines telling the proponent what to assess.
assessment_method_label: Completeness or conformity check against written criteria
assessment_method_note: Deliberative scoping against a published draft, open to comment. The same framing move as route selection, done in the open.
kind_label: Framing — fixes what later steps can argue about
note: The pairing with route selection is the cleanest comparison on this map.

name: Federal or joint panel
legal_basis: NuPPAA s.94(1)(a)(ii)–(iii) and ss.160–162, with the record public under s.123(2).
takes_in: The whole project, including the Manitoba segment.
can_produce: A panel report.
decider: Minister of Environment, or joint appointment
assessment_method_note: Panel hearing over the whole project, including the Manitoba segment.
note: The only body anywhere on this map with a mandate over the full 1,200 km corridor.

name: Review and public hearing
legal_basis: NuPPAA s.102, under which the hearing is discretionary and may be closed; s.103 factors include (c) the priorities and values of the residents and (f) cumulative effects.
takes_in: The impact statement, technical review, submissions and oral testimony.
can_produce: Findings.
public_record: Yes, though a hearing may be closed
assessment_method_note: Hearing against a mandatory list of factors, with traditional knowledge admissible under s.103(3). The only method anywhere here that names residents' values as something to be considered.
note: Section 103(c) makes residents' priorities and values a mandatory statutory factor. Nothing in Manitoba law has an equivalent.

name: Licensing decision
legal_basis: The Environment Act ss.11 and 12; s.12.0.1 requires proponent consultation to be considered and s.12.0.2 requires climate to be considered.
takes_in: The assessment record, departmental comments, the consultation record, and any Commission report.
can_produce: Licence with conditions, or refusal.
assessment_method_note: Judgment on the record against two named statutory factors. How those are weighed against anything else is not specified and not published.
note: Everything becomes one answer here. Section 12.0.2 gives climate a statutory foothold no other value in this Act enjoys.

name: Minister's decision and certificate
legal_basis: NuPPAA ss.105–111, reconsideration under s.112. Override grounds are limited to national or regional interest, or to terms being insufficient or excessively onerous. Section 107(1) requires the Board to reconsider in light of the Minister's reasons. Section 108 permits the Minister to vary terms that are purely socio-economic.
takes_in: The Board's report.
can_produce: Accept or reject terms; override; issue a certificate.
assessment_method_note: Judgment on the Board's report, with enumerated override grounds — except for socio-economic terms, which s.108 allows the Minister to vary without stating one.
note: The sharpest thing on this map. Socio-economic considerations are mandatory at review under s.103(c), then singled out at s.108 as the one class of term a Minister may vary without stating a ground.

name: Water licence
legal_basis: Nunavut Waters and Nunavut Surface Rights Tribunal Act, s.37 coordinating it with the Review Board.
takes_in: Water use and waste deposit.
can_produce: A licence with conditions.
assessment_method_note: Technical standards and licence conditions.
note: Whether a transmission corridor triggers it at all is unconfirmed.

name: Inuit Owned Land access
legal_basis: The Nunavut Agreement. The relevant articles and the association's lands policy have not been retrieved.
takes_in: Applications to use Inuit Owned Land parcels.
can_produce: Permit or lease with terms, or refusal.
decider: The regional Inuit association, as landowner
assessment_method_note: Negotiation between landowner and proponent. Whatever is traded against what leaves no public trace — and this may be where the most consequential combining actually happens.
note: NuPPAA defines a regulatory authority as a public body, so the s.75 gate may not bind a private landowner — while s.74 still prohibits carrying out the project before assessment.

name: Archaeology permit
legal_basis: Territorial archaeological and palaeontological site regulations. Not retrieved.
takes_in: Proposed ground disturbance.
can_produce: A permit with conditions.
assessment_method_note: Standards and permit conditions.
note: Unverified. No party in the record has raised heritage as a concern.

name: Fisheries Act authorisation
legal_basis: The Fisheries Act. The provision has not been confirmed.
takes_in: Works likely to harmfully alter fish habitat.
can_produce: Authorisation with offsetting, or refusal.
assessment_method_note: Habitat standards with offsetting requirements. One value, assessed well, and nothing else admitted.
note: Subject to the Nunavut screening gate, which binds federal authorities in the territory.

name: Migratory Birds Act
legal_basis: The Migratory Birds Convention Act 1994. Inferred.
takes_in: Works affecting birds or nests.
can_produce: No project permit; constraints on timing.
assessment_method_note: Prohibitions and timing windows rather than an assessment.
note: Unverified.

name: Notice of Alteration
legal_basis: The Environment Act s.14 (alteration of a licensed development).
takes_in: A licensee's description of a proposed change to a licensed development.
can_produce: Approval of a minor alteration (licence amended, e.g. 3285 R), or a direction to file a new proposal.
public_record: Partial — approvals are posted; the request often is not
assessment_method_note: The Director decides whether a change is minor enough to approve without a new proposal. No public comment period is required for a minor alteration.
note: Added 8 Oct 2026 to record mineral-project histories (Wanipigow, Tanco, Minago, MacLellan). Legal basis to be confirmed by Eric.

name: Appeal to the Minister
legal_basis: The Environment Act s.27 (appeal of a Director's decision to the Minister).
takes_in: Written appeals from anyone affected by a licence decision.
can_produce: Appeal dismissed, or the licence varied or revoked.
assessment_method_note: Appeal goes to the minister whose department issued the licence. No independent tribunal.
note: Added 8 Oct 2026 for the Tanco licence appeals. Legal basis to be confirmed by Eric.

name: Federal environmental / impact assessment
legal_basis: Canadian Environmental Assessment Act 2012 (projects begun before 28 Aug 2019) or the Impact Assessment Act; triggered by the Physical Activities / Project List regulations.
takes_in: Environmental impact statement, public and Indigenous comments, agency analysis.
can_produce: Decision statement with binding conditions, or a finding of unjustified significant effects.
decider: Minister of Environment and Climate Change (Governor in Council if effects are significant)
assessment_method_note: Whether the project is likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects, after mitigation.
note: Added 8 Oct 2026 for the Lynn Lake gold project (decision statement March 2023). Distinct from fed-cer, which is the Energy Regulator route for the Kivalliq line.
